_doc: Per-lane freshness and plausibility checks. A breach logs a journal record with the sink's
MSGID_LANE_STALE, so it lands in the same incident queue as a systemd unit failure and the
This exists because the unit-failure queue only sees units that FAIL. Five of the analyst's
first sixteen findings were the other class: a lane that kept exiting 0 while going quietly
wrong — notifications silent for 57 h after a flat phone battery, local news 78% unenriched for
21 days, Ultrahuman coverage down to 4 h/day, Amex alerts arriving with no amount in them, the
statement archive ending in a false cliff. Green unit, degenerate data, nobody notified.
CAVEAT on the training lanes: a lane that is stale and an operator who did not train look
identical from here. Their windows are deliberately generous, and a breach means 'go and look',
Only lanes whose layout has actually been verified are listed. Declaring a path nobody checked
is the very failure this file is meant to catch — mail and local-news enrichment are absent for

lanes.name: notifications
lanes.note: The estate's only live Amex source. Went silent 57.1 h on 2026-07-29 (flat phone).

lanes.name: amex-alert-detail
lanes.note: Bare 'There was a transaction on your card ending with 11005.' carries no amount, so spend is unrecoverable from this lane. Bare since 2026-08-06.

lanes.name: ultrahuman
lanes.note: Ring data. `date` is written by the fetcher's own loop, so an empty 200 still yields a dated row — without `require` this lane reads ok on a table with no measurement in it. The five fields are payload-borne and independent: hr_points alone would be too strict (20 of 143 real days have none while still carrying steps/vo2_max). Coverage collapse is a separate problem, held by ultrahuman-coverage.

lanes.name: technogym-cardio
lanes.note: Generous window: no training is indistinguishable from a stalled fetch.

lanes.name: ultrahuman-coverage
lanes.note: Every day was PRESENT with a sleep summary while the HR series behind it was truncated to ~4 h. A row count cannot see that; this can.
